reading.body:
A founding OpenAI CTO launched Thinking Machines Lab in February 2025 to build collaborative, multimodal AI systems that work with people rather than pursuing full autonomy.

Murati's departure from OpenAI after nearly six years, including a stint as interim CEO during the November 2023 board crisis, marked a shift in focus within the AI leadership class. Her new company's stated philosophy centers on human-AI collaboration rather than systems designed for independent operation. This represents a distinct position in the market at a time when debate over AI autonomy remains unresolved.

The company's emphasis on multimodal systems and collaboration means Thinking Machines Lab operates in a narrower technical scope than the large-scale model training that dominates compute infrastructure discussion. The data provided does not specify the company's compute requirements, funding, facilities, or power consumption, making it impossible to assess how its technical approach translates to infrastructure demands. What the company prioritizes and how those priorities affect resource intensity remain separate questions.

The cases include Bass v. OpenAI, United States v. OpenAI OpCo, JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC, GRANT v. OPENAI INC, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, Vredenburgh v. OpenAI OpCo, and The Seattle Times Company v. OpenAI Inc. Buist v. Anthropic, PBC is also filed and monitored, with no development recorded. No case names Thinking Machines Lab or Murati directly in the records supplied. No planned listing, funding round, or valuation for Thinking Machines Lab is recorded. The next recorded step, if any, would be a development in those monitored dockets.
standing.record: The site's records on Murati add up to two company affiliations and a set of lawsuits that mostly involve OpenAI. OpenAI is listed as a startup in San Francisco, founded in 2015, with no funding or valuation recorded, and Thinking Machines Lab is listed as a startup in San Francisco, California, founded in 2025, also with no funding or valuation recorded. The lawsuits include Bass v. OpenAI, United States v. OpenAI OpCo, JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC, GRANT v. OPENAI INC, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, Vredenburgh v. OpenAI OpCo, and The Seattle Times Company v. OpenAI Inc. One further case, Buist v. Anthropic, PBC, names Anthropic rather than OpenAI. Every listed case is marked as filed, with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker. The pattern is that legal exposure in these records clusters around OpenAI, while Thinking Machines Lab has no case listed.
standing.standing: Mira Murati stands in the records as the founder and CEO of Thinking Machines Lab, a public benefit corporation founded in 2025 and launched publicly on February 18, 2025. The site also lists OpenAI as a company where she is an executive, after nearly six years there, including her rise to Chief Technology Officer in May 2022. She served briefly as interim CEO of OpenAI on November 17, 2023, during the board crisis following Sam Altman's departure. She announced her departure from OpenAI on September 25, 2024. Her current company is described as focused on collaborative, multimodal AI systems. The records give no funding or valuation for Thinking Machines Lab, so the scale of what she controls is not shown.
